reuse.why: Holiday moves go through the existing applyWeekendRule, but the daily-skip rule is not put there: getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange each compute isDailyWithWeekendSkip and filter on their own, and the two app.ts copies redo the holiday match inline instead of using isNonWorkingDay.

duplication.why: The daily-skip flag, the oversampling 'take 8' and the weekend/holiday filter are written three times, with the holiday matching rewritten inline in two of them (and without the MM-DD form).

placement.why: Part of the weekend rule lives in shared applyWeekendRule and part in the handlers in server/schedules/app.ts, so date-resolution policy leaks into the server handler layer.

scope.why: Changes stay within schedule date logic, the new handler, the type and tests.

maintainability.why: Changing what counts as a skipped day means editing four places that already disagree (the inline app.ts checks ignore MM-DD holidays), and applyWeekendRule gained an odd fallback branch to getDateWithSkippedWeekend.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange (server/schedules/app.ts) and getNextDate (shared/schedules.ts) decide daily weekend/holiday skipping themselves instead of through applyWeekendRule/WeekendRule.

disguised_duplication.where: The non-working-day test exists as isNonWorkingDay in shared/schedules.ts and again as inline `!d.isWeekend(date) && !config.holidays?.includes(dayFromDate(date))` filters in getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange.

abstraction_drift.where: WeekendRule/applyWeekendRule gained a holidays field and a fallback branch to getDateWithSkippedWeekend for unknown modes; getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange each implement daily skipping outside it.
